study type: Experimental animal study (conditional knock-out mouse model)
outcome: delay in ossification along the fusion area of secondary palatal bones
decreased phosphorylation of GSK3beta at Ser-9
cohort: The study utilized conditional knock-out mouse embryos to investigate the physiological function of the GSKIP protein.
finding: GSKIP deficiency caused lethality at birth, respiratory distress, and incomplete palatal shelf closure in mice, primarily due to decreased phosphorylation of GSK3beta at Ser-9 leading to enhanced GSK3beta activity.
